drivingQuestion: Why would a court seek grounds to acquit an inciter, whom the Torah forbids sparing?
outcomeNote: Ulla's own answer (ties to the government) resolves his difficulty

segments.he: אָמַר עוּלָּא: וְתִסְבְּרָא? יֵשׁוּ הַנּוֹצְרִי בַּר הַפּוֹכֵי זְכוּת הוּא? מֵסִית הוּא, וְרַחֲמָנָא אָמַר: ״לֹא תַחְמֹל וְלֹא תְכַסֶּה עָלָיו!״ אֶלָּא שָׁאנֵי יֵשׁוּ, דְּקָרוֹב לְמַלְכוּת הֲוָה.
segments.en: «Ulla said: And» how can «you understand» this proof? Was «Jesus the Nazarene worthy of» conducting «a search» for a reason to «acquit» him? «He» was «an inciter» to idol worship, «and the Merciful One states» with regard to an inciter to idol worship: «“Neither shall you spare, neither shall you conceal him”» (Deuteronomy 13:9). «Rather, Jesus was different, as he» had «close» ties «with the government,» and the gentile authorities were interested in his acquittal. Consequently, the court gave him every opportunity to clear himself, so that it could not be claimed that he was falsely convicted.
